headline: Govt says no prospect of return for Shakib after event with Hasina
summary: Youth and Sports Minister Aminul Haque states there is no longer any room for flexibility regarding the former captain's return to Bangladesh.
details: Youth and Sports Minister Aminul Haque announced that former Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib Al Hasan has no prospect of returning to play after joining a media event with ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina.
The Minister stated that while the government had previously been flexible and tolerant, his appearance alongside the former leader has changed the situation, leaving no room for further flexibility.
Shakib, 39, joined the New Delhi event virtually on Wednesday, which marked the second anniversary of the student-led uprising that toppled the previous government.

In a separate interview with Reuters, Shakib expressed readiness to return to Bangladesh from his two-year exile to face trial on murder and corruption charges if the government guarantees his safety.
The cricketer has been living in the United States since August 2024 and hopes to play a farewell series at home and represent Bangladesh in the 2027 one-day World Cup.
Shakib claims he has written to multiple ministries seeking to have charges against him dropped, describing them as fabricated, and expressed a desire to speak with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

He also revealed that a previous attempt to return in late 2024 collapsed after he was told to turn back mid-journey from the airport lounge, and another attempt failed after a social media post for Hasina.
Shakib noted that his bank accounts have been frozen for 18 months and that he has not seen his parents, who remain in Bangladesh, for two years.
caption:
No way back? The government says Shakib Al Hasan has no prospect of returning to play for Bangladesh.

Youth and Sports Minister Aminul Haque announced that former Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib Al Hasan has no prospect of returning to play after joining a media event with ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina.

The Minister stated that while the government had previously been flexible and tolerant, his appearance alongside the former leader has changed the situation, leaving no room for further flexibility.

Shakib, 39, joined the New Delhi event virtually on Wednesday, which marked the second anniversary of the student-led uprising that toppled the previous government.

In a separate interview with Reuters, Shakib expressed readiness to return to Bangladesh from his two-year exile to face trial on murder and corruption charges if the government guarantees his safety.

The cricketer has been living in the United States since August 2024 and hopes to play a farewell series at home and represent Bangladesh in the 2027 one-day World Cup.

Shakib claims he has written to multiple ministries seeking to have charges against him dropped, describing them as fabricated, and expressed a desire to speak with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

He also revealed that a previous attempt to return in late 2024 collapsed after he was told to turn back mid-journey from the airport lounge, and another attempt failed after a social media post for Hasina.

Shakib noted that his bank accounts have been frozen for 18 months and that he has not seen his parents, who remain in Bangladesh, for two years.

headline_marked: Tarique Rahman [[tortured at JIC cell]] during 1/11 period: ICT Chief Prosecutor
headline: Tarique Rahman tortured at JIC cell during 1/11 period: ICT Chief Prosecutor
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal chief prosecutor stated that Tarique Rahman was detained and tortured at the Joint Interrogation Cell during the military-backed caretaker government.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam revealed that Tarique Rahman was detained and tortured at the Joint Interrogation Cell (JIC) during the 1/11 period under the military-backed caretaker government.
The statement was made after a visit to the JIC, an alleged secret detention facility located at the DGFI headquarters in Dhaka.
The inspection was conducted by tribunal judges, prosecution, and defence lawyers to investigate facilities where victims of enforced disappearances were allegedly held and tortured.

Two crimes against humanity cases involving enforced disappearances are currently being tried before the tribunal against deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina and several former and serving army officers.
Other alleged secret detention facilities mentioned by the prosecution include a site at Kochukhet and another at the Rab-1 headquarters in Uttara.
The chief prosecutor argued that site visits are essential for a fair trial, citing similar practices by international tribunals for Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia.
According to the tribunal's Rules of Procedure, judges have the authority to inspect any location they deem necessary in the interest of justice.
caption:
Tarique Rahman was detained and tortured at the JIC cell during the 1/11 period, according to the ICT Chief Prosecutor.

The statement was made after a visit to the JIC, an alleged secret detention facility located at the DGFI headquarters in Dhaka.

The inspection was conducted by tribunal judges, prosecution, and defence lawyers to investigate facilities where victims of enforced disappearances were allegedly held and tortured.

Two crimes against humanity cases involving enforced disappearances are currently being tried before the tribunal against deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina and several former and serving army officers.

Other alleged secret detention facilities mentioned by the prosecution include a site at Kochukhet and another at the Rab-1 headquarters in Uttara.

The chief prosecutor argued that site visits are essential for a fair trial, citing similar practices by international tribunals for Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia.

According to the tribunal's Rules of Procedure, judges have the authority to inspect any location they deem necessary in the interest of justice.
